jurisdictions.name: Australia
jurisdictions.primary_law: No AI Act. Existing laws plus Guidance for AI Adoption; mandatory requirements for Commonwealth agencies from 15 June 2026
jurisdictions.enforcing_body: Existing regulators (OAIC, ACCC, eSafety and others); Australian AI Safety Institute
jurisdictions.summary: Australia shelved mandatory guardrails and a standalone AI Act, relying instead on existing privacy, consumer, copyright and discrimination law. An Australian AI Safety Institute launched in early 2026 with AUD 29.9 million. From 15 June 2026 Commonwealth agencies face the first mandatory AI requirements, including impact assessments and Chief AI Officers, with full compliance due by 10 December 2026. Voluntary guidance consolidates ten guardrails into six practices.
jurisdictions.one_line: Australia decided not to pass an AI law and instead relies on existing laws; government agencies face new AI rules.

jurisdictions.name: Brazil
jurisdictions.primary_law: Bill PL 2338/2023 (AI Legal Framework): passed Senate December 2024, pending in Chamber of Deputies
jurisdictions.enforcing_body: Proposed National AI Regulation and Governance System (SIA); ANPD enforces LGPD
jurisdictions.max_penalty: Proposed: up to R$50 million per infraction
jurisdictions.summary: Brazil's PL 2338/2023, modelled on the EU AI Act, would set risk tiers (unacceptable, high, lower), rights to explanation and contestation, and a national governance system with fines up to R$50 million. The Senate approved it unanimously in December 2024; in the Chamber a special committee has held hearings but, as of August 2026, awaited the rapporteur's report after at least four missed vote dates. Scores here reflect protections currently in force, mainly the LGPD data protection law.
jurisdictions.one_line: Brazil is close to passing an EU-style AI law but it has stalled in Congress; for now privacy law is the main protection.

jurisdictions.name: Canada
jurisdictions.primary_law: No federal AI statute. AIDA (Bill C-27) died on 6 January 2025; Bills C-34 and C-36 (June 2026) are pending
jurisdictions.enforcing_body: Privacy commissioners and sector regulators; provinces
jurisdictions.max_penalty: Varies by statute; none AI-specific at federal level
jurisdictions.summary: Canada has no federal AI law. AIDA lapsed with Bill C-27 on 6 January 2025. In June 2026 the government tabled Bill C-34 (a Digital Safety Act covering some AI chatbots and synthetic content) and Bill C-36 (privacy reform with duties on automated decision systems). The voluntary generative AI code (27 September 2023), Quebec Law 25 and Ontario job-posting disclosure (1 January 2026) fill part of the gap.
jurisdictions.one_line: Canada has no national AI law yet; protections come from privacy rules, some provincial laws and voluntary codes.

jurisdictions.name: China
jurisdictions.primary_law: Layered CAC regulations: Recommendation Algorithms (2022), Deep Synthesis (2023), Generative AI Interim Measures (2023), AI-Generated Content Labelling Measures (2025)
jurisdictions.enforcing_body: Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC) with MIIT, MPS and others
jurisdictions.max_penalty: Under PIPL: up to RMB 50 million or 5% of annual revenue; criminal liability for serious offences
jurisdictions.summary: China regulates AI through targeted administrative rules rather than one comprehensive statute: recommendation algorithms (in force March 2022), deep synthesis (January 2023), generative AI (15 August 2023) and mandatory explicit and implicit labelling of AI-generated content from 1 September 2025. Providers with public opinion influence must complete security assessments and filings before launch. Ethics review measures (December 2023) cover AI research enterprises.
jurisdictions.one_line: In China the state sets the rules on AI: AI content must be labelled and companies must file their systems with regulators.

jurisdictions.name: European Union
jurisdictions.enforcing_body: EU AI Office, national competent authorities
jurisdictions.max_penalty: €35 million or 7% of global annual turnover
jurisdictions.summary: The EU AI Act is the world's first comprehensive horizontal AI law, applying a risk-tiered classification system to all AI systems placed on the EU market or used within it, regardless of where the provider is based. It prohibits outright a set of unacceptable-risk applications, imposes extensive conformity assessment obligations on high-risk systems, and introduces a novel governance regime for general-purpose AI (GPAI) models above compute thresholds.
jurisdictions.one_line: The EU has passed the world's most comprehensive law controlling how AI can be used — it bans some uses outright and requires companies to justify high-stakes AI decisions that affect you.

jurisdictions.name: India
jurisdictions.primary_law: India AI Governance Guidelines (voluntary, 5 November 2025) plus IT Rules synthetic media amendment (effective 20 February 2026) and DPDP Act 2023
jurisdictions.enforcing_body: Ministry of Electronics and IT (MeitY); Data Protection Board (once constituted)
jurisdictions.max_penalty: IT Rules: loss of safe harbour for intermediaries; DPDP penalties (sources disagree on maximum)
jurisdictions.summary: India has no standalone AI law. MeitY issued voluntary AI Governance Guidelines (reported as 5 November 2025) that reject pre-approval of models, with a conversion pathway to mandatory rules reportedly due around November 2026. Binding duties come from the IT Rules amendment on synthetic content (G.S.R. 120(E), effective 20 February 2026: labelling, provenance metadata, three-hour takedown) and the DPDP Act with its November 2025 Rules.
jurisdictions.one_line: India relies on voluntary guidelines for AI, with firm rules on deepfake labelling and data protection.

jurisdictions.name: Japan
jurisdictions.primary_law: Act on Promotion of Research, Development and Utilization of AI-Related Technologies (AI Promotion Act, Act No. 53 of 2025)
jurisdictions.enforcing_body: AI Strategic Headquarters (Cabinet); sector ministries; Personal Information Protection Commission
jurisdictions.max_penalty: No direct penalties under the AI Promotion Act; APPI fines up to JPY 100 million for specified offences
jurisdictions.summary: Japan's AI Promotion Act (in force 1 September 2025) is a basic, promotion-oriented law with no penalties. It created an AI Strategic Headquarters chaired by the Prime Minister and requires national AI Basic Plans: the first was adopted on 23 December 2025 and a second on 14 July 2026. Business conduct is guided by the METI and MIC AI Guidelines for Business (April 2024); authorities can investigate, advise and publicly name non-compliant firms.
jurisdictions.one_line: Japan encourages responsible AI through guidance and national plans rather than strict rules or fines.

jurisdictions.name: Kenya
jurisdictions.primary_law: Artificial Intelligence Bill, 2026 (published; not enacted). Kenya National AI Strategy 2025–2030; Data Protection Act 2019
jurisdictions.enforcing_body: Proposed Office of the AI Commissioner; Office of the Data Protection Commissioner
jurisdictions.summary: Kenya's Artificial Intelligence Bill, 2026 (reported 17 June 2026) would create a risk-based regime with pre-deployment risk and human rights impact assessments for high-risk systems, human oversight, explainability, labelling of AI-generated likeness, workforce impact assessments, and an independent AI Commissioner. It is not law. Scores reflect protections in force, chiefly the Data Protection Act 2019.
jurisdictions.one_line: Kenya has published a rights-focused AI bill but it is not yet law; data protection law is the main safeguard.

jurisdictions.name: Singapore
jurisdictions.primary_law: No standalone AI law. Model AI Governance Frameworks (incl. Agentic AI, January 2026), AI Verify, sector guidance
jurisdictions.summary: Singapore entered 2026 without a standalone AI law. It governs through voluntary frameworks: the Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI (IMDA, January 2026, updated May 2026), the AI Verify testing toolkit, an AI Tester Accreditation Programme planned for Q3 2026, and MAS's AI risk management handbook (March 2026) for finance. Data centre growth is rationed through the IMDA Green Data Centre Roadmap (30 May 2024).
jurisdictions.one_line: Singapore guides AI through voluntary frameworks and testing tools rather than a single AI law.

jurisdictions.name: South Korea
jurisdictions.primary_law: Act on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and Establishment of Trust (AI Basic Act)
jurisdictions.max_penalty: Administrative fines up to KRW 30 million (about US$21,000); corrective orders including service suspension
jurisdictions.summary: South Korea's AI Basic Act took effect on 22 January 2026, making it the second comprehensive national AI law after the EU's. It sets duties for high-impact AI (health, energy, transport, hiring, biometrics), labelling for generative AI, extra safety duties for very large models (10^26 FLOPs per an MSIT notice), and extraterritorial reach. Penalties are modest and a one-year fine grace period has been signalled.
jurisdictions.one_line: South Korea now has a binding AI law that makes companies label AI content and take extra care when AI affects your health, job or rights.

jurisdictions.name: Switzerland
jurisdictions.primary_law: Federal Council AI regulatory strategy (12 February 2025): sector-specific approach and ratification of the Council of Europe AI Convention
jurisdictions.enforcing_body: Federal Department of Justice and Police and sector regulators; Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner
jurisdictions.summary: On 12 February 2025 the Federal Council chose a sector-specific, technology-neutral approach and rejected an EU-style horizontal AI law. Its priority is to ratify the Council of Europe AI Convention, with a consultation draft expected by end 2026, plus non-binding measures such as self-declaration frameworks. Ratification needs parliamentary approval and may face a referendum.
jurisdictions.one_line: Switzerland will not copy the EU's AI Act; it plans to adopt the Council of Europe treaty and adjust sector laws.

jurisdictions.name: United Arab Emirates
jurisdictions.primary_law: No federal AI law. PDPL (Decree-Law 45/2021), National AI Strategy 2031, DIFC Regulation 10 (AI, January 2026)
jurisdictions.enforcing_body: UAE Data Office; DIFC Commissioner; sector regulators (CBUAE, DFSA, FSRA, DHA)
jurisdictions.max_penalty: PDPL fines up to AED 5 million; DIFC Regulation 10: US$25,000 to 50,000 per violation
jurisdictions.summary: The UAE has no single AI law; a federal framework has been discussed but not enacted. Governance is layered: the federal PDPL (full compliance due 1 January 2027), non-binding strategy and ethics guidance, a 2024 Child Digital Safety Law, and DIFC Regulation 10 (in force January 2026), which requires AI impact assessments and transparency for high-risk uses by DIFC entities.
jurisdictions.one_line: The UAE has no single AI law; rules differ between the federal government, free zones and sectors.

jurisdictions.name: United Kingdom
jurisdictions.primary_law: Pro-Innovation AI Regulation White Paper + AI Security Institute
jurisdictions.enforcing_body: Existing sector regulators (FCA, ICO, CMA, Ofcom) + AI Security Institute
jurisdictions.summary: Post-Brexit, the UK has deliberately chosen not to pass comprehensive horizontal AI legislation, instead relying on existing sector regulators to address AI harms within their domains. The 2023 White Paper established five cross-cutting principles — safety, security and robustness; appropriate transparency and explainability; fairness; accountability and governance; contestability and redress — but these are not legally binding. The AI Security Institute focuses exclusively on frontier model safety evaluation, not on consumer protection or rights.
jurisdictions.one_line: The UK has chosen not to pass a single AI law — instead existing regulators in each industry are responsible for keeping AI in check, which means your protections depend on which sector you're in.

jurisdictions.name: United States
jurisdictions.summary: The US has no comprehensive federal AI law. Governance is fragmented across sector-specific agencies, voluntary frameworks (NIST AI RMF), and a growing patchwork of state legislation. EO 14110 was revoked in 2025. Executive Order 14365 (11 December 2025) set up a DOJ task force to challenge state AI laws and calls for a federal preemption bill; Congress has not passed one. Colorado reenacted a narrower AI Act (SB 26-189) effective 1 January 2027; California SB 53 is in force.
jurisdictions.one_line: The US has no single national AI law — your protections depend entirely on which state you live in and which industry is using AI on you.

jurisdictions.name: Vietnam
jurisdictions.primary_law: Law on Artificial Intelligence (passed 10 December 2025; in force 1 March 2026)
jurisdictions.enforcing_body: Ministry of Science and Technology and designated state management authority
jurisdictions.max_penalty: Administrative sanctions to criminal liability; amounts set by Government decree
jurisdictions.summary: Vietnam's first standalone AI law, passed on 10 December 2025 and in force from 1 March 2026, is risk-based: high-risk systems need conformity assessment before deployment, medium-risk systems carry transparency and labelling duties, and low-risk systems face minimal rules. It adds machine-tagging of generated media, serious-incident reporting through a national AI portal, a national AI database and a sandbox, with transition periods of 12 or 18 months for existing systems.
jurisdictions.one_line: Vietnam now has a binding AI law that sorts AI by risk and requires labelling of AI-made media.
